# Exceptions to identifiers.py. Each one is a value that belongs to no
# deployment, with the reason it is safe to publish. Adding a line here is a
# reviewable decision, which is the point of keeping the list in the repository.
#
#   allow <regex>          a value that matches it entirely is not a finding
#   ignore <glob> <regex>  in files matching glob, text matching regex is not scanned
#
# Comments after a value start with two spaces and a hash.

# The account console. Every Azure Databricks customer uses the same host.
allow accounts\.azuredatabricks\.net
allow accounts\.(cloud|gcp)\.databricks\.com

# Azure built-in role definitions. Their ids are the same in every tenant and
# Microsoft publishes them; infra/bootstrap/main.identity.tf needs them for the
# ABAC condition. Checked with `az role definition list --name <role>`.
allow acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7  # Reader
allow ba92f5b4-2d11-453d-a403-e96b0029c9fe  # Storage Blob Data Contributor

# Addresses that reach no one. The .invalid domain is reserved by RFC 6761 for
# examples. GitHub's noreply addresses are what it publishes in place of a real
# one, and noreply@github.com commits every merge made in its web interface.
allow [A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@([A-Za-z0-9-]+\.)*invalid
allow ([0-9]+\+)?[A-Za-z0-9-]+(\[bot\])?@users\.noreply\.github\.com
allow noreply@github\.com
# Dependabot signs off every commit it writes with GitHub's support address.
allow support@github\.com

# Provider checksums. They are random base64 and hex, so over enough provider
# upgrades one will contain a run of digits between two '/' or '+' characters,
# or the letters of a token prefix, by chance alone. Blanking them first means a
# provider upgrade can never fail the gate on noise, while the rest of every
# lock file is still scanned.
ignore **/.terraform.lock.hcl (h1|zh):[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+
